feature: Measurement chips, arrow captions and shape strokes stay crisp when you zoom in
summary: Zooming past 100 percent used to sharpen the words you had placed but leave everything else behind: the number on a measurement, the caption on an arrow and the stroke of a shape were still a document-sized picture blown up. Now they are drawn at the size you are looking at them, so a readout you zoom in to read is as sharp as the label beside it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to turn on: the Experiments flag "Words stay sharp when you zoom in" is on by default.

try.do: Press I for Measure and drag a distance measurement across something.
Press A for Arrow, drag an arrow at something, type a caption and press Return.
Press Escape to drop the selection.
Zoom to about 300 percent with Command + and wait about a second.
Read the number in the measurement chip and the words in the arrow's caption.
Keep going to 800 percent and look at the caliper's rounded corners and the arrowhead.

evaluate: At 300 percent, does the number in the chip read as sharp as the app's own panel text on the right?
Does the sharp copy arrive fast enough after you stop zooming, or do you notice the soft moment first?
The screenshot underneath still goes square and blocky past 2x while the chips and arrows are now smooth. Does that mix read as deliberate or as two different pictures?
At 800 percent a 1px caliper line is now a smooth 8 pixel line rather than a hard block. Does it still read as one image pixel to you?
Is there anything else on the canvas that still goes soft when you zoom that should not?
rough: The sharp copy is drawn about 90 milliseconds after you stop zooming, so there is still a brief soft frame. That delay was already there for labels and this change does not touch it.

A shape stretched across a whole 12 megapixel capture is left alone: redrawing it at 8x would ask for a bitmap tens of times the size of the document, so it falls back to the old blown-up look. A shape drawn at the size of the thing it points at, which is every normal one, is redrawn.
Gradient fills inside a shape are still painted small and stretched. A gradient has no hard edges to lose, so nothing looks softer for it.

Shot 1 is a real screen capture from a scripted probe run at about 316 percent. Shots 2 and 3 are two real captures of the same walk, before and after the change, cropped and placed side by side so the difference is visible at a glance.
The layer border a style draws was already sharp: Core Image draws it around the magnified box. It now has a test guarding that.
